description: Forward paper-trading ledgers for two pre-registered overnight strategies: ON1 (Nikkei 225 micro futures, long-only overnight) and ONR (J-REIT ETF 1343, long-only overnight). Both are fully rebuilt from their source CSVs on every run (deterministic, no hidden state) -- see docs/PREREG_on1_forward.md and docs/PREREG_onr_forward.md.
source: ON1: data/jpx_daily/nk225_sessions.csv (scripts/fetch_jpx_daily.py) -> scripts/paper_on1.py. ONR: data/onr/etf_1343_daily.csv (Yahoo chart API) + data/onr/reit_index_daily.csv (kabutan code=0105) -> scripts/paper_onr.py
retention: kept indefinitely; ON1/ONR ledgers are the ON1/ONR live-tracking record itself, not a re-derivable cache -- do not treat as disposable even though the build is deterministic from inputs, because the INPUT daily CSVs are refreshed/self-healed in place and old ledger rows can differ from what a fresh rebuild from today's inputs would produce for the same date

entry_date.meaning: day-session date the position was entered (closing-auction print of the central month)

exit_date.meaning: next trading day's day-session opening-auction print date

month.meaning: contract delivery month traded (central month = largest day-session volume that day; entry and exit use the same month)

entry_px.meaning: central-month day-session closing-auction print used as entry

exit_px.meaning: central-month day-session opening-auction print, next trading day, used as exit

gross_bps.meaning: (exit_px - entry_px) / entry_px in bps, before fees

fee_yen.meaning: round-trip fee, fixed 11 yen/contract/side x2 = 22 yen
fee_yen.notes: constant by construction, not measured per trade

net_bps.meaning: net_yen expressed back in bps of entry_px*multiplier

large_entry_px.meaning: the LARGE (regular, non-micro) Nikkei 225 futures print at the same entry moment, for diagnostic comparison

large_exit_px.meaning: large-contract print at the same exit moment

micro_minus_large_entry.meaning: micro print minus large print at entry -- a slippage/tracking diagnostic, NOT a cost charged in net_yen (the PREREG charges only the fixed fee, no slippage)

note.meaning: free-text annotation, e.g. reason a day was skipped upstream

date_entry.meaning: closing-auction (15:30 JST) date the ETF was bought
date_entry.unit: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYYMMDD (see source script for exact format)

date_exit.meaning: next trading day's opening-auction (9:00 JST) date

dividend_yen.meaning: dividend credited, only when exit date is the ex-dividend date (overnight holder is entitled)

pnl_yen.notes: fee is 0 by PREREG (auction print, no slippage charge in the paper model)

index_on_bps.meaning: TSE REIT index overnight return in bps, for attribution against etf_on_bps

gap_bps.notes: blank when either leg's index row is missing -- tolerated, never blocks the ETF-only trade from being recorded

cum_pnl_yen.meaning: running cumulative pnl_yen from the ledger start

mean_bps.meaning: mean of etf_on_bps across the ledger

gap_mean_bps.meaning: mean of gap_bps across rows where it is not blank

guard.meaning: PREREG sec.3 warn/stop guard state evaluated on the ledger's rolling window
guard.notes: guard percentile thresholds are duplicated from a frozen one-time computation over backtest_data/reit_onr_20260904/etf_1343_daily.csv (n=4399), not recomputed live

last_date.meaning: most recent date_exit in the ledger

known_defects: ON1 ledger silently SKIPS (never back-fills) any day with a missing central-month print -- a gap in entry_date is a real skip, not necessarily a data-collection failure; cross-check data/jpx_daily/nk225_sessions.csv before calling it a defect

ONR ledger only starts at date_entry >= 2026-09-04 (freeze date per PREREG sec.1) even though the underlying etf_1343_daily.csv history goes back to 2008-09-16 -- earlier history is intentionally never backfilled into the ledger

both ledgers are FULLY REBUILT from source CSVs on every run -- if the source daily CSV (data/onr/etf_1343_daily.csv, data/jpx_daily/nk225_sessions.csv) is corrected/self-healed for an already-ledgered date, the ledger row for that date changes silently on the next run; the intake ledger's md5 history is what lets you detect that a source file changed between two runs

ONR guard thresholds are a frozen constant duplicated in both paper_onr.py and docs/PREREG_onr_forward.md by design (so the dashboard renders even if one changes independently) -- a mismatch between the two copies is itself a bug worth surfacing, not a false alarm
